requirement: A published site's robots.txt goes out no-store, so an edge cache cannot keep it after the site is unpublished

oracle.ref: PR #1181 (fix); fix evidence: Measured 11/10/2026: curl -sI https://business-joomla.tracy.site/robots.txt answered cache-control: max-age=14400, cf-cache-status: HIT; the origin (tracy-web on dev) sent no cache-control for Joomla and public, max-age=86400 for EmDash. A draft site's robots.txt (tracy-web, no-store) answers cf-cache-status: BYPASS.
oracle.invariant: Every 'R-1:' test reports ok: a proxied /robots.txt answers cache-control: no-store whether the CMS sent public, max-age=86400 (EmDash), nothing (Joomla/Apache), an Expires or CDN-only lifetime headers, on GET and HEAD, on the Tracy address and on a customer's own domain; any other file keeps the CMS's cache header (pre-fix: the CMS header went out unchanged).
oracle.productSourcesScope: file-level: the files the case imports, reads or runs (declaration line, or the first code line); the invariant is exercised through them, the executed assertion is the case command

writes: run dir under QA_ARTIFACT_ROOT: logs/, tmp/<case> (the child TMPDIR, removed after the run)

assertionIds: R-1: a published robots.txt the CMS marks public for a day (EmDash) goes out no-store
R-1: a published robots.txt with no cache header at all (Joomla/Apache) goes out no-store
R-1: an Expires the CMS sets on robots.txt does not outlive the no-store
R-1: a CDN-only lifetime header (read by the edge before Cache-Control) is dropped
R-1: HEAD answers the same cache header as GET
R-1: on a customer own domain (issue 1037) the projected robots.txt is no-store too
R-1: any other file keeps the cache header the CMS chose
